channel.title: Dodge recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Dodge Durango rear spoiler may come off in traffic
item.description: The trim piece across the top of the rear window isn't lined up right with the roof, so opening and closing the rear hatch can damage it. A damaged spoiler can break off while you're driving and land in the road, where it becomes a hazard for the cars behind you. Dealers will inspect it and repair or replace it and realign the hatch, free. Note: if your Durango was fixed under an earlier recall, it needs this repair too.

item.title: Dodge Hornet rear seat belts may not retract properly
item.description: The rear seat belts on the outer seats can get twisted inside the mechanism that pulls the belt back in. When that happens, the belt does not wind up the way it should and may not sit correctly against the person wearing it. A belt in that condition may not hold someone properly in a crash. Dealers will replace the retractor — the spring-loaded reel that takes up the slack in the belt — at no charge to you.

item.title: Dodge Charger EV and Jeep Wagoneer S display failure
item.description: A software error can make the main display screen behind the steering wheel fail. That screen is what tells you which gear the car is in and shows warning lights for the brakes, tire pressure, stability control, and airbags. If it goes blank, you could miss an important warning or not know whether the car is in drive or reverse. A dealer reloads the display software during a normal service visit.

item.title: Rollx Wheelchair Vans: Restraints May Not Lock Wheelchair
item.description: These are vans converted by Rollx for wheelchair use. The straps that hold a wheelchair use retractors, which work like a seat belt: they pull in slack and then lock so the chair cannot roll. On these vans, the QRT-Deluxe and QRT-Max retractors may fail to lock. If they do not lock, the wheelchair and the person in it can shift or slide while the van is moving, which raises the risk of injury. Rollx and the restraint maker will check the retractors and replace them if needed.

item.title: Dodge Charger and Jeep Wagoneer S electrics may roll away
item.description: In these electric vehicles, a spring inside the unit that drives the wheels may have been put in wrong. Because of that, the vehicle may not truly stay in Park when you move the gear selector to P, and it can roll away on its own. The vehicle also does not meet the federal rule meant to prevent rollaways. A dealer will replace the electric drive module at no charge to you.

item.title: Ram ProMaster and Dodge Journey backup camera may fail
item.description: A tiny computer chip inside the backup camera can crack. When it does, the picture behind the vehicle may not show up properly on the screen as you reverse, so you could miss a person or object behind you. Chrysler will replace the camera at no cost, but the parts are not ready yet. The letter mailed September 30, 2025 is only a warning; a second letter with the actual fix is expected around July 2026.

item.title: Dodge Charger EV may not make required pedestrian warning sound
item.description: Electric cars run almost silently, so they are required to make an artificial sound at low speeds to warn people nearby. On these cars, the amplifier that plays that sound may be missing part of its software, so the car may make no outside sound at all. Someone walking or biking near you may not hear the car coming. A dealer will load the correct software into the amplifier free of charge.

item.title: Dodge Hornet backup camera image may not appear
item.description: When you shift into reverse, the dashboard screen may not show the picture from the backup camera. The camera itself is not the problem; the display can fail to bring the image up, so you see a blank screen instead of what is behind you. Federal rules require a working rear view image, so these vehicles do not meet the standard. A dealer will load new software into the display, or replace the display if the software does not fix it.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee, Dodge Durango brake module failure
item.description: A fault in the antilock brake computer can switch off both antilock braking and the stability control that keeps you from sliding in a turn. It can also make your brake lights come on when you are not braking, and it can let you start the vehicle and shift out of Park without your foot on the brake — so the vehicle could roll away. Dealers will replace a brake sensor and update the software, free. Vehicles already fixed under the earlier recall 22V-426 need this new repair too.

item.title: Dodge Hornet brake pedal can collapse while driving
item.description: On certain Dodge Hornet SUVs, the arm of the brake pedal can collapse under your foot. If that happens, you lose the ability to slow down or stop the vehicle with the brake pedal. The fix is to reinforce the pedal arm so it cannot give way. Chrysler mailed letters to owners in October 2024. Any Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep or Ram dealer can do the repair, and it does not cost you anything.

item.title: Dodge Charger left rear seat back may not lock
item.description: On these Dodge Chargers, the left rear seat back may not lock in the upright position the way it should. The catch that holds it in place may not grab properly, so the seat back can move or fold forward when it is supposed to stay put. You probably would not notice anything wrong during normal driving. A dealer will check the latch piece and adjust it so the seat locks securely again.

item.title: Dodge Challenger left rear seat back may not lock
item.description: In these Dodge Challengers, the left rear seat back may not lock upright as intended. The part it latches onto can be slightly out of position, so the seat back may not stay firmly in place. Nothing about the way the car drives will feel different, and you may not spot the problem yourself. A dealer will inspect the latch and adjust it so the rear seat back locks and holds the way it should.

item.title: Jeep, Ram, Chrysler backup camera may show nothing
item.description: The radio software in these vehicles can keep the backup camera picture from appearing at all. When you shift into reverse, the screen may not show what is behind you, so you cannot see a child, a person, or an object in the vehicle's path while backing up. That makes it much easier to hit something you never saw. The repair is a software update for the radio, done at the dealer or sent to the vehicle wirelessly.

item.title: Dodge Durango and Ram trucks lose stability control
item.description: A software error in the computer that runs the anti-lock brakes can switch off the electronic stability control system. Stability control senses when the vehicle is starting to slide or spin in a turn and automatically brakes individual wheels to help you stay on course. With it shut off, you still have normal brakes and steering, but you lose that automatic help. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule that requires stability control to work.

item.title: Dodge Hornet label missing tire and wheel size
item.description: The sticker that lists your tire and wheel size is missing that information on some 2024 Dodge Hornet and Alfa Romeo Tonale vehicles. That label is what a tire shop or a mechanic looks at when replacing a wheel or a tire. Without it, someone could install a wheel that is the wrong size for your car. A wheel that does not match can change how the car handles and stops, which could lead to a crash.

item.title: Dodge Charger and Chrysler 300 Curtain Airbags May Rupture
item.description: On certain Dodge Charger and Chrysler 300 cars, the side curtain airbags that run above the side windows were built with a defect. The metal canister that fills the bag with gas can burst instead of inflating the bag the way it should. If that happens, sharp pieces of metal can fly into the passenger area and strike the people inside. Dealers will replace both the right and left side curtain airbags at no cost to you.

item.title: Dodge Hornet sticker lists wrong maximum load weight
item.description: Certain 2023-2024 Dodge Hornet and Alfa Romeo Tonale vehicles have the wrong number printed on the tire information sticker, the label in the driver's door opening that tells you how much weight the vehicle can carry. Because the number is wrong, an owner could load in more people and cargo than the vehicle is built to handle. An overloaded vehicle handles and stops poorly. A dealer puts a corrected label over the old one.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Charger, Challenger parking brake may not hold
item.description: The parking brake on these cars may not have been adjusted correctly when they were built. That means the brake may not hold the car the way it should, and the car can roll away after you park it. Because of this, the vehicles also do not meet the federal safety rule for light vehicle brakes. A dealer will adjust the parking brake properly, and the work is free. Owner letters went out in late February 2024.

item.title: Dodge Hornet may lack warning sound when backing up
item.description: Hybrid and electric vehicles run so quietly that federal rules require a small speaker to make a sound when the vehicle is in reverse, warning people nearby. On these vehicles that speaker may be missing altogether, or its plug may have come loose, so nothing sounds when you back up. Someone walking behind you may not realize the vehicle is moving and could be struck. A dealer will check the connection and secure or replace the plug or speaker.

item.title: Dodge Durango Pursuit shifter can slip out of gear
item.description: Some 2023 Dodge Durango Pursuit police models have the gear shifter mounted on the dashboard instead of the console. The rubber boot around that shifter can rub against it and push it out of gear while you are driving. If that happens, the engine stops sending power to the wheels and the vehicle coasts, even though the motor is still running. Chrysler's fix is a new shifter boot, installed at the dealer at no cost.

item.title: Dodge Hornet loose battery cables can cause fire
item.description: Two power cables in your plug-in hybrid Hornet — the positive cable on the regular 12-volt battery and the cable connector for the high-voltage battery — may not have been tightened enough at the factory. A loose connection can get very hot and start a fire, whether the car is parked or moving. Park outside and away from buildings until a dealer checks both connections and tightens them, which is free.

item.title: Dodge Durango rear spoiler can come loose
item.description: The spoiler across the back roof of your Durango may not have been lined up correctly with the roof. Each time the rear hatch is opened and closed, that misalignment can damage the spoiler. A damaged spoiler can eventually break free and fall off while you are driving, landing in the road behind you where another driver could hit it. A dealer will inspect the spoiler and put on a new one if needed.

item.title: Dodge Charger, Durango shifter may slip out of drive
item.description: Certain 2022 Dodge Charger and Durango vehicles have a shifter assembly that was not heat-treated correctly, so the metal is not as strong as it should be. Because of that, the shifter may not fully catch in the "drive" position. It can slip out of drive on its own, and the vehicle would suddenly stop pulling while you are on the road. Dealers will replace the shifter assembly free of charge.

item.title: Dodge Charger, Challenger, Chrysler 300 tire pressure sensors fail
item.description: These Dodge Challenger, Dodge Charger, and Chrysler 300 cars have small sensors in the wheels that watch your tire pressure. The batteries inside those sensors can die early, so a sensor stops working. Then the car cannot warn you when a tire is actually low. Worse, if the warning light is already lit because of a dead sensor battery, you may ignore it and miss a real low tire. Driving on a low tire can cause it to fail.

item.title: Dodge Journey Side Reflector Is Too Dim
item.description: The headlight units on some 2017-2018 Dodge Journey SUVs contain a small amber reflector on the side. That reflector is supposed to bounce back the light from other cars' headlights so your vehicle shows up from the side, even when it is parked or its own lights are off. On these vehicles the reflector is too dim to do that job properly. The dealer will replace the whole headlight assembly on each side at no cost.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Charger, Challenger tire pressure sensors quit early
item.description: These cars have sensors in the wheels that watch your tire pressure. The battery inside a sensor can die too early, so the sensor stops working. When that happens, the system will not warn you that a tire is going low. Worse, if the warning light is already on because of a dead sensor battery, it can hide a real low-tire problem. A low tire can fail while you drive. Dealers will check the sensors and replace any bad ones.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee and Durango can roll out of Park
item.description: A fault in the antilock brake computer can turn on your brake lights and let the vehicle start and shift out of Park even when your foot is not on the brake pedal. That means the vehicle can be moved out of Park by accident and roll away on its own, with no warning, possibly hitting someone nearby. Chrysler replaced this recall with a newer one, number 24V838, so even a vehicle already repaired needs the new fix.

item.title: Dodge Durango and Jeep Grand Cherokee can lose engine power
item.description: These SUVs have a valve that routes some exhaust back into the engine to cut pollution. On these vehicles the valve can stick open. When that happens the engine can suddenly stop making power, so the vehicle slows or quits pulling with no warning, which is dangerous if you are merging, passing, or climbing a hill. There is no way for you to see it coming. The dealer replaces the whole valve assembly at no cost to you.

item.title: Dodge Durango steering may bind or fail suddenly
item.description: The steering rack is the gear assembly that turns your front wheels when you turn the wheel. A bar inside it may not have been hardened enough during manufacturing, so it can bind, or stick, inside the rack. When that happens the steering can feel very hard to turn, or you can lose steering control altogether, which can cause a crash. A dealer will replace the whole steering gear assembly at no charge to you.

item.title: Ram and Durango stability control warning light may not work
item.description: Certain Ram 2500 and 3500 trucks and Dodge Durango SUVs have a software problem in the anti-lock brake computer. Because of it, the dashboard warning light for the electronic stability control — the system that helps keep the vehicle from skidding or spinning — may not light up when that system has a problem. So you could be driving with the stability system not working and never be told about it. Dealers will update the software free of charge.

item.title: Dodge Durango rear spoiler may come loose
item.description: On some 2021 Durango SUVs, the spoiler — the trim piece across the top of the rear window — may not line up properly with the roof. Because of that, opening and closing the rear liftgate can knock into the spoiler and damage it over time. A damaged spoiler can eventually work loose and fall off while you are driving, landing in the roadway where another vehicle could hit it or swerve to avoid it.

item.title: Dodge Challenger dashboard warning lights too dim to see
item.description: On some 2021 Dodge Challengers, the warning and status lights in the dashboard cluster don't light up brightly enough. That means the small symbols that tell you whether things like your airbag or brake system are working properly can be hard or impossible to see, day or night. The dashboard software was built with the wrong version, so the brightness is off. A dealer can reload the correct software into the cluster, and it costs you nothing.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Challenger, Charger windshield may not be glued properly
item.description: When these cars were built, the glue that holds the windshield in place may not have bonded properly. The windshield looks and works normally in everyday driving, but in a crash it could separate from the car instead of staying put, which can lead to injuries. Because of this, the vehicle does not meet the federal safety rule for windshield mounting. Your dealer will remove the old sealant, put in new sealant and refit the windshield, free of charge. Letters were mailed August 31, 2021.

item.title: Dodge Durango side curtain airbag bolt loose or missing
item.description: On certain Dodge Durango SUVs, a bolt that holds the side curtain airbag in place may be loose or missing entirely. That airbag is the long one that drops down from the roof beside the windows. If the bolt is not holding properly, the airbag may not open the way it was designed to during a crash, so it may not protect people as well as it should. A dealer will tighten or replace the fastener free of charge.

item.title: Jeep, Ram, Chrysler backup camera image stays on screen
item.description: The software in your 8.4-inch or 12-inch radio screen has a bug. After you back up and shift out of reverse, the picture from the backup camera can stay on the screen instead of switching back to the normal display. That means you can be driving forward while a rear-facing picture is still showing, which can pull your eyes and attention off the road ahead. The fix is a software update for the radio screen.

item.title: Dodge Charger Pursuit backup camera blanks in stealth mode
item.description: Some Dodge Charger Pursuit police cars have a setting called stealth mode, which turns off the lights and screens so the car is less noticeable at night. The problem is that when stealth mode is on, the backup camera picture does not appear on the screen when you shift into reverse. That means you back up with no camera view, and you cannot see a child, a person, or an object behind the car.

item.title: Modified Dodge Grand Caravan fuel pump gasket can leak
item.description: Vantage Mobility is recalling certain Vantage-modified 2016-2019 Dodge Grand Caravan vans. The gasket that seals the fuel pump to the fuel tank can break down over time and allow gasoline to leak out. Leaking fuel near anything hot or sparking can start a fire. Vantage will supply the parts and pay a repair shop to replace the fuel tank gasket, and will reimburse owners who have the work done.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango can lose power suddenly
item.description: The front differential — the gearbox that sends power to the front wheels — on these 2019 Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango SUVs may contain gears that were not hardened enough. The teeth on those gears can wear away. If they wear off completely, the vehicle can suddenly lose power while you are driving. It can also lose the PARK function, meaning the vehicle may not stay put when you park it. Dealers replace the whole front differential.

item.title: Dodge Grand Caravan rear seat anchors may fail in crash
item.description: The metal latches that anchor the rear seats to the floor are held on by welds that may not be strong enough. The welds on the outer second-row seats can fail in a front-end crash, and the ones on the third-row bench can fail in a rear-end crash. The second-row bench and bucket seats also may not hold up to the required loads, so a seat or its belt may not hold someone in place.

item.title: Dodge Challenger and Charger Wrong Wheels Can Damage Tires
item.description: These cars left the factory with front wheels and brakes that do not fit together properly. Because of the mismatch, the front tire can rub against the steering knuckle, the metal part the wheel is mounted on. That rubbing damages the tire, and a damaged tire can lose air all at once while you are driving. The dealer will put on new front wheels, check the tires and replace any that are damaged, and check the alignment.
